subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & pricing — AuroraAI request for concession
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@auroraai.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@auroraai.com, Tom Li <tom.li@auroraai.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing & pricing — AuroraAI requirements

Karthik,

Thanks again for the helpful demo last week. We ran the workload profiling you suggested and attached the forecast. High level: we expect a sustained 12K RPS token throughput for 6 months with peaks approximately 2x for short bursts. Our security/compliance team requires a reserved/private GPU pool with predictable throughput and an SLA for token latency percentiles.

Budget is constrained for Q3 — we need to explore a committed reserved pool but will need either a step-down pricing schedule or an upfront credit if we sign a 12‑month reserved commit. Can Redwood provide a concession (credits or deeper % discount) to match a competitor that quoted a 22% effective reduction when amortized across committed units?

I attached our forecast and a short requirements doc. Would like to understand:
- Recommended GPU pool size and expected p90 token latency at our forecasted load
- Commitment tiers you would propose for a 12-month reserved contract
- Any available one-time credits or strategic discounts (exec approvals?) to meet the competitor price band

Appreciate a quick turn — procurement would like a term sketch before EOW.

Regards,
Elena Park
Head of ML Ops
AuroraAI

Attachments: AuroraAI_Demand_Forecast.xlsx (xlsx), AuroraAI_MA_Platform_Requirements.pdf (pdf)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@auroraai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & pricing — AuroraAI requirements

Elena — thanks for the forecast and requirements. High level response below; detailed numbers attached.

- Recommended starting pool: 8 x A100-equivalent nodes with automatic burst headroom to handle 2x peaks. That maps to the throughput you quoted with p90 token latency in the 120–180ms range depending on prompt length and KV cache hit rate.
- Commitment options (12-month):
  * Bronze: 8 nodes reserved — standard list pricing
  * Silver: 12 nodes reserved — 10% off list
  * Gold: 16 nodes reserved + burst — 18% off list + discounted preemptible burst credits

We can offer a one-time strategic credit but that requires exec sign-off for anything >$150k in credits. I’m looping in Marissa on this thread to coordinate a short concession request and the finance impact. I’ve also attached our internal pricing grid.

Can we set a short call tomorrow to align on the latency SLOs and finalize the set of metrics to include in the term sketch?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: dedicated-pricing-grid-20270510.xlsx (xlsx)

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena@auroraai.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & pricing — AuroraAI requirements

Elena / team — quick note from the pricing desk.

We reviewed the forecast. AuroraAI is strategic from a vertical and reference standpoint; reasonable path to match competitor economics if Aurora commits to the gold tier (16 nodes) and a 12-month reserved contract. Options:

1) Structured credit: one-time credit amortized over the contract term to achieve ~20% effective reduction vs list. Requires exec approval if credit > $150k.
2) Hybrid discount + tiered ramp: moderate upfront discount (12–15%) + additional usage-based credits for the first 3 months. No exec required under $80k.

Ben — can you run an alternate P&L for the two options and flag the exact credit threshold that needs priyom approval? I want the finance-backed recommendation before we surface a number to Elena.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

No attachments here.

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & pricing — AuroraAI requirements (finance analysis)

Marissa / Karthik — attached is the finance memo. Summary:
- To reach an effective ~20% reduction for the 12-month Gold tier we need to provide a $220k one-time credit amortized monthly.
- If we structure as hybrid (13% upfront discount + 3-month usage credits) the finance impact is ~$95k and falls under Marissa's delegated approval.

Given Aurora’s strategic fit, recommend proposing the hybrid structure first (low risk, faster approval). If Aurora pushes for parity with competitor we can escalate to Priyom for the $220k credit for approval.

Priyom — requesting quick guidance: would you approve an exception for the $220k credit for a strategically-significant reference account at your discretion? If yes, state any guardrails (e.g., additional case studies, logo use, 12-month net revenue minimum).

Ben Carter
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference

Attachment: approved-credit-memo-auroraai.pdf (pdf)

From: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@auroraai.com>, procurement@auroraai.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & pricing — AuroraAI requirements (approval)

Team / Aurora — after reviewing the memo and strategic rationale I approve the one-time credit request at $220,000 under the following conditions:

1) AuroraAI signs a 12-month Gold commitment (16-node reserved pool) within 10 business days.
2) Redwood receives an executive case study commitment (public or private briefing) and a joint blog post within 90 days; marketing review to be confirmed.
3) Credit will be applied as a one-time invoice credit, amortized monthly; finance to record as contra-revenue.

Karthik — please draft the updated term sketch and share the updated pricing and SLO language. Marissa / Ben — confirm the credit accounting mechanics and any cap on burst usage that could materially affect cost.

Priyom Das
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
